latin.692: §. II. Assertionis Reformatæ Rationes, in triplici Classe dispositas exhibebimus, quarum PRIMA Auctoritate divina; ALTERA Auctoritate humana, seu Ecclesiasticâ, divinam interpretante; TERTIA denique Ratione, per Scripturam S. informatâ, i. e. divina Consequentia, nititur.
latin.693: CLASSIS PRIMÆ Argumentum primum suppeditat Institutionis S. Cœnæ Historia, quâ Christus cum duodecim discipulis suis, mensæ S. accubuisse fertur, unô eorum impio existente & Domini sui nefariam proditionem meditante Luc. 22. 14. coll. cum vers. 3. Hunc, primum S. Epuli indignum Convivam, Corpus Christi neutiquam manducasse, vel istius ullo modo participem factum esse, inde constat, quod acceptô à Christo obsonio, seu intincto, Paschalis convivii, Cœnam antecedentis, frustulo, Satanas in ipsum intrasse dicitur Joh. 13. 27. nullam cum Christo ejusque corpore communionem habens 2. Cor. 6.
latin.694: Cum hujus verò indigni convivæ primi conditione, reliquorum similium omnium, Spiritualium Christi proditorum, i. e. impiorum atque Infidelium hypocritarum Conditionem prorsus eandem esse, dubitare non sinit, specie eadem horum, cum Judæ perversione, malitia, eundem obicem omni cum Christo communioni positura.
latin.695: Unde sequitur alterum primæ classis argumentum, Historiæ Institutionis S. Cœnæ, de Juda Conviva impio, & ob impietatem suam destinatam, communionis cum Christo planè incapaci, interpretativum ac confirmativum Apostolicum, quod Communionem cum Diabolis foventes (quale quid in omnes impios cadere Apostolus Johannes testatur 1. Ep. 1, 6. cap. 3. vers. 6. 8. 9.) omni communionis cum Christo possibilitate excludit 1. Cor. 10, 21. Non potestis poculum Domini bibere & poculum dæmoniorum. Non potestis Mensæ Domini participes fieri, & mensæ dæmoniorum.
latin.696: Accedit Tertium Argumentum, indignè manducantes, indignitate actuali & restrictâ, sibi judicium temporale edere & bibere 1. Cor. 11, 29. 30. 31.; Sicque pari modo, indignitate habituali & absolutâ manducantes indignè, sibi edere & bibere judicium spirituale.
latin.697: Perque consequens, non Christi carnem & sanguinem edere bibereque, cùm caro Christi spiritualiter vivificet, sanguis verò Christi spiritualiter purget, i. e. purget ab omni peccato Joh. 6. 53. & 1. Joh. 1, 7. hosque effectus semper & absque restrictione, his locis, dicantur producere, quandocunque scil. quispiam, actu, eorum particeps redditur.
latin.698: Ut nequicquam hic excipiatur, distinguendo inter participationem corporis & sanguinis Christi corporalem, & spiritualem, utpote distinctionem hanc restrictivam Scriptura S. prorsus ignorante, quin potius absolutè & citra restrictionem asserente: Omnem eum, qui carnem Christi edit & sanguinem Christi bibit, manere in Christo, & Christum in eo, habereque vitam æternam, Joh. 6. vers. 54. 56.

pass_a.692: §. II. We shall exhibit the Reasons of the Reformed Assertion arranged in a threefold Class, of which the FIRST rests on divine Authority; the SECOND on human or Ecclesiastical Authority interpreting the divine; and the THIRD finally on Reason informed by Holy Scripture, i.e. divine Consequence.
pass_a.693: Of the FIRST CLASS the first Argument is supplied by the History of the Holy Supper’s Institution, in which Christ is said to have reclined at the sacred table with his twelve disciples, one of them being impious and meditating nefarious betrayal of his Lord (Lk 22:14 coll. v. 3). That this first unworthy Guest of the Sacred Feast in no way ate Christ’s Body, or was made partaker of it in any mode, is clear from this: that when he had received from Christ the morsel — the dipped bit of the Paschal feast preceding the Supper — Satan is said to have entered into him (Jn 13:27), having no communion with Christ and his body (2 Cor 6).
pass_a.694: But that with this first unworthy guest’s condition the Condition of all the rest like him — Spiritual betrayers of Christ, i.e. the impious and Infidel hypocrites — is entirely the same, is not left in doubt: the same species of these, with Judas’s perversion and malice, will set the same obstacle to every communion with Christ.
pass_a.695: Whence follows the second argument of the first class, interpretive and confirming of the Institution History concerning Judas the impious Guest, plainly incapable of communion with Christ because of his destined impiety — the Apostolic word that those fostering Communion with Devils (such as the Apostle John testifies falls on all the impious: 1 Jn 1:6; 3:6, 8, 9) are excluded from every possibility of communion with Christ (1 Cor 10:21): You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot be partakers of the Lord’s Table and of the table of demons.
pass_a.696: A Third Argument is added: those eating unworthily with actual and restricted unworthiness eat and drink temporal judgment to themselves (1 Cor 11:29–31); and so in like manner those eating unworthily with habitual and absolute unworthiness eat and drink spiritual judgment to themselves.
pass_a.697: And consequently they do not eat and drink Christ’s flesh and blood — since Christ’s flesh spiritually vivifies, and Christ’s blood spiritually purges, i.e. purges from all sin (Jn 6:53; 1 Jn 1:7), and these effects are said in these places always and without restriction to be produced whenever anyone is actually made partaker of them.
pass_a.698: So that nothing may be excepted here by distinguishing corporal and spiritual participation of Christ’s body and blood — inasmuch as Holy Scripture utterly ignores this restrictive distinction, and rather asserts absolutely and without restriction: that everyone who eats Christ’s flesh and drinks Christ’s blood abides in Christ, and Christ in him, and has eternal life (Jn 6:54, 56).

692: §.II lays out Reformed reasons for the assertion in three classes.
First: divine authority. Second: human/church authority interpreting the divine. Third: reason informed by Scripture — divine consequence.
693: Class I, argument 1: at the Supper’s institution Christ reclines with the Twelve, one impious and plotting betrayal (Lk 22:14 with v.3).
That first unworthy guest did not eat Christ’s body in any mode: after the dipped Paschal morsel, Satan entered him (Jn 13:27) — no communion with Christ and his body (2 Cor 6).
694: Every spiritual betrayer — impious and unbelieving hypocrites — shares the same condition: the same malice sets the same block to all communion with Christ.
695: Class I, argument 2 confirms the Judas history from the Apostles: those who keep communion with demons are shut out from any communion with Christ.
John marks that state in all the impious (1 Jn 1:6; 3:6, 8–9); Paul: you cannot drink the Lord’s cup and demons’ cup, or share the Lord’s table and demons’ table (1 Cor 10:21).
696: Class I, argument 3: those who eat unworthily with actual, limited unworthiness eat and drink temporal judgment (1 Cor 11:29–31).
By parity, those who eat unworthily with habitual, absolute unworthiness eat and drink spiritual judgment.
697: Therefore they do not eat and drink Christ’s flesh and blood.

For his flesh spiritually vivifies and his blood spiritually purges from all sin (Jn 6:53; 1 Jn 1:7) — and those effects always follow, without restriction, whenever anyone is actually made a partaker.
698: No escape by splitting corporal vs spiritual participation: Scripture does not know that restrictive distinction.
It asserts without limit that whoever eats the flesh and drinks the blood abides in Christ and has eternal life (Jn 6:54, 56). Stop §.II before §.III (patristic class).

notes.694: Same condition for all spiritual betrayers.
notes.697: Vivify/purge entail not eating if judged.
